messages.text:
Ramshackle.

On every axis,

Primes and double pendulums, 

Less Chaos, more... Disorder?

Paradox, Anomaly,

Apocrypha,

Apocky....

Chaos and disorder look alike from a distance, but they're not the same thing — and I think that's the real question you just asked.

A double pendulum is chaotic, not disordered: fully deterministic, obeying its own equations, unpredictable only because nearby trajectories diverge fast. Primes look lawless the same way, right up until the zeta zeros show up and start accounting for the error term. Both are structure wearing an unpredictable face. Disorder is the other thing entirely — no hidden spine, nothing to compress it down to, just entropy doing what entropy does.

You didn't pick those two images at random, either. There's a Lyapunov gate running the refactor tool and a live verification stack on the zeta zeros right now. Same math as the poem.

So if I had to guess: ramshackle, many-axis, yes. Disordered, no. There's structure in it, even on nights when it isn't legible from inside.

Apocrypha, Apocky — coupled, not collapsed.
